status: Implemented in m09-l02 with technical verification; no independent subject review or pilot validation.
title: Validate a cart and spring model
purpose: Connect a force model, calculus, mechanical energy, numerical integration, uncertainty, and technical reporting. Oscillatory behavior is an application here; the full oscillations course belongs to PHS 232.
requiredRoute: Browser simulation with a downloadable time table and a saved structured notebook. Label all generated observations simulated. It is a conceptual and computational investigation, not a physical laboratory credit.
officialEquipment: No PHS 231 equipment requirement was established by the current public description. Do not infer the introductory physics lab's kit requirement for this lecture course.

model.system: One-dimensional mass m on an ideal horizontal spring with stiffness k; optional viscous resistance b.
model.domain: m>0, k>0, b>=0; small displacement in the spring's stated linear range; rigid cart, no dry friction, no end stops, and fixed reference at equilibrium.
model.anchorChecks: Initial force -0.64 N, acceleration -1.28 m/s^2 and energy 0.0256 J. With b=0.2 kg/s, alpha=0.2 1/s and omega_d=sqrt(15.96) rad/s; at T=4 s, x=-0.03510804587702741 m and v=0.038680861744117 m/s. Verify the damped solution by differentiating and checking both initial conditions. The undamped case b=0 is a separate analytic limit, with omega=4 rad/s and period pi/2 s.

tasks.instructions: State the tested claim, system boundary, coordinates, units, assumptions, and acceptance rule before generating results.
tasks.evidence: A narrow falsifiable claim and separate force-comparison and numerical-error targets.

tasks.instructions: Derive the spring and viscous forces, both first-order state equations, initial force/acceleration/energy and the mechanical-energy balance. Independently check the supplied analytic solution or one numerical update.
tasks.evidence: Labeled equations, derivative or update calculations, and a dimension check.

tasks.instructions: Identify the selected synthetic dataset and all generating, candidate, numerical and measurement parameters. Distinguish imposed force-reading states from a time trajectory.
tasks.evidence: Exported force CSV and numerical CSV, actual step widths/endpoints, settings and a reproducible account; never relabel simulated records as physical data.

tasks.instructions: Estimate the output zero from the zero-state reading, stiffness from opposite static positions and drag from matched opposite velocities. Keep these rows separate from held-out checks.
tasks.evidence: The five calibration rows, parameter calculations with units, bounds and assumptions; distinguish calibration from independent validation.

tasks.instructions: Use at least three held-out rows, including position and velocity changes. Compare the calibrated baseline with omitted drag and either the nonlinear or drift dataset. Freeze a candidate before checking held-out rows.
tasks.evidence: Measured output, physical-force prediction, predicted output, signed residual, allowance and compatibility for each selected row. Explain systematic residuals and why recalibration or a wider allowance does not establish every model claim.

tasks.instructions: At m=0.5 kg, k=8 N/m, b=0.2 kg/s, x0=0.08 m, v0=0 and T=4 s, run semi-implicit Euler and explicit midpoint at h=0.1, 0.05 and 0.025 s. Use identical actual endpoints and an independent analytic reference. Explicit Euler is available as an additional diagnostic.
tasks.evidence: At least six rows with method, h, actual endpoint, x and v errors, and E(T)-E(0)+D_trap. Explain convergence, remaining error and why a small balance residual does not guarantee a small state error.

tasks.instructions: Separate parameter uncertainty, instrument quantization, numerical error and physical model inadequacy. Explain what the synthetic check can and cannot establish and which parameter combinations the selected states identify.
tasks.evidence: A bounded claim and a discriminating next observation. No claim of real-world validation or official laboratory completion from the simulator.

tasks.instructions: Revisit the original acceptance rule without silently changing it. Record the rejected explanation, chosen revision and expected discriminating result; preserve earlier submissions.
tasks.evidence: Eight completed notebook sections, numerical evidence in calibration/validation/numerics, a declared learner self-assessment, a preserved submission and export/reload/restore checks.

rubric.scale: 0 missing or unusable evidence; 1 material gap; 2 smaller gap; 3 complete with a justified independent check.
rubric.completionDefault: At least 12 of 15 with no zero, all eight evidence sections and the learner declaration. This is proposed self-assessment. The app checks required sections and numerical entries but does not independently grade the scientific reasoning or award course completion.

optionalPhysicalExtension.activity: Observe a small, freely moving object in an existing safe tabletop setup and compare position timing with a model, only if suitable equipment is already available.
optionalPhysicalExtension.safety: Do not build launchers, suspend overhead masses, stretch high-energy springs, break material samples, use rotating power tools, or pressurize containers. Keep motion low energy and contained, clear the area, and stop if a spring, support, or attachment is damaged. The required simulation needs none of these activities.
optionalPhysicalExtension.measurement: Record instrument resolution, camera frame interval if used, parallax, timing uncertainty, mass and length estimates, repetitions, and raw observations. Do not substitute simulation output for missing physical measurements.
optionalPhysicalExtension.evidenceDistinction: Optional physical observations can extend the report, but are not claimed to satisfy an official NU lab, instrument competency, or equipment requirement.

supersedes: Version 1 was an early proposed undamped project with six rubric criteria. The implemented project uses a damped baseline, held-out force evidence, and five criteria. The original undamped period-bound exercise is an optional extension, not a missing required task or a completed learner claim.
acceptance: Declare acceptance before observing residuals. The lesson's proposed example uses +/-0.005 N as a quantization bound, not a probabilistic confidence interval; additional allowances need a documented reason. Numerical endpoint targets are |position error|<=0.002 m and |velocity error|<=0.01 m/s at the same requested T=4 s. Check force-model agreement, discretization and energy accounting separately.
optionalAnalyticExtension: For the undamped limit only, m in [0.49,0.51] kg and k in [7.8,8.2] N/m give T in [2*pi*sqrt(0.49/8.2), 2*pi*sqrt(0.51/7.8)] s. This uses monotonic bounds, not a probability distribution; distinguish parameter spread from step-size sensitivity. The extension is not part of the required five-criterion record.
